def merge_intervals(intervals):
    if not intervals:
        return []
    intervals = sorted(intervals, key=lambda x: x[0])
    merged = [intervals[0]]
    for start, end in intervals[1:]:
        last_start, last_end = merged[-1]
        if start <= last_end:
            merged[-1][1] = max(last_end, end)
        else:
            merged.append([start, end])
    return merged

assert merge_intervals([[1,3],[2,6],[8,10],[15,18]]) == [[1,6],[8,10],[15,18]]
assert merge_intervals([[1,4],[4,5]]) == [[1,5]]
assert merge_intervals([]) == []

After a 20% discount
$$P_{1}=P\,(1-0.20)=0.80\,P$$

A 25% increase on the discounted price
$$P_{2}=P_{1}\,(1+0.25)=1.25\,P_{1}=1.25\times0.80\,P=1.00\,P$$

$$P_{2}=P$$

The two successive percentage changes cancel. In general
$(1-0.20)(1+0.25)=1$, so the net change is $0\%$. The final price is the same as the original, e.g. $100\to 80\to 100$.
